name: Pull-up bar
lead: A pull-up bar is a fixed horizontal bar from which the user hangs to perform pull-ups, chin-ups and hanging exercises. Bars are sold for doorway mounting, wall or ceiling mounting, and as freestanding frames. The pull-up is an upper-body strength exercise in which the body is suspended by the hands, usually gripping the bar wider than shoulder width, and pulled up so that the elbows move toward the torso [1].

For appearance, the bar is a low-cost way to train the back and arms. The exercise loads the latissimus dorsi, trapezius and biceps brachii and is widely used as a measure of upper-body strength, endurance and strength-to-weight ratio [1]. In looksmaxxing discussion, pull-up bars are associated with building back and shoulder width (the 'V-taper'), which proponents say makes the waist appear narrower in proportion and improves how clothes fit. The chain is: a bar at home, regular pulling sessions, more back and arm muscle, a broader-looking upper body.

Research on pull-ups consists mainly of electromyography studies comparing variations rather than trials of physique outcomes. A 2010 study compared pull-up and chin-up variations in trained adults [2], and a 2017 study compared traditional, suspension and towel pull-ups in 15 resistance-trained adults [3]. Wikipedia reports that overall muscle activation was similar across grip variants [1]. A 2026 analysis of United States emergency department data estimated about 41,000 visits for pull-up bar injuries over ten years [4].

chain: Hang from a bar at home or outdoors
Pull the body up with the lats, traps and biceps working
Progress repetitions or load over time
More back and arm muscle gives a wider-looking upper body and a V-shaped torso
angle.text: The bar itself does not change appearance; it is the equipment for vertical pulling, one of the main ways bodyweight and gym trainees train the lats and upper back. Proponents say the resulting back width makes the shoulders look broader relative to the waist.

infobox: Doorway (tension or frame), wall, ceiling, freestanding
Pronated (pull-up), supinated (chin-up), neutral grip, weighted, assisted [1]
About $25 to $40; a forum user reports about $8 for a basic bar [8]

paras: From a hanging position the body is pulled up vertically and then lowered until the arms and shoulders are fully extended. The top position may be chin over bar or higher [1]. The pull-up is a closed-chain compound movement involving elbow flexion and shoulder adduction or extension [1]. Pull-ups are usually done on a bar, but towels, rotating handles, gymnastics rings or joists can be used [1].

Grips can be pronated, supinated (commonly called a chin-up) or neutral. Wikipedia reports that when participants choose their own grip width it is typically 20 to 50 percent wider than shoulder width, and that a very wide grip could increase injury risk or reduce repetitions by lengthening the lever arm [1][14].

Variations listed by Wikipedia include weighted pull-ups with a belt or vest, one-arm versions, mixed grip, chest-to-bar pull-ups, eccentric (slow lowering) pull-ups, assisted pull-ups using bands, counterweights, machines or foot support, kipping pull-ups that use a swing, and the muscle-up, which transitions from a pull-up into a dip and originated in gymnastics [1].

Hanging and pulling from bars is part of calisthenics, a bodyweight training tradition with roots described in ancient Greece and Han dynasty China, with 19th-century physical-education programs and, from the late 1950s, Royal Canadian Air Force exercise plans that helped spread fitness culture. Modern calisthenics uses pull-up bars, parallel bars, rings and parallettes, and outdoor parks often include bars free for public use [11].

Street workout is the modern outdoor form. Wikipedia dates the YouTube era of the movement to 2005, when videos by groups and individuals gained tens of millions of views, and says athletes such as Hannibal For King rose to fame and inspired people worldwide. Competitions include freestyle bar routines and streetlifting, which tests weighted pull-ups or chin-ups and dips. The World Street Workout & Calisthenics Federation is based in Riga and the World Calisthenics Organization in Los Angeles [11][12].

In fitness testing, pull-ups have been correlated with job tasks in firefighting, policing and the military and used as conditioning for climbing, gymnastics, rowing and swimming. Some programs accepted a flexed-arm hang as a substitute because few female recruits could do a pull-up [1]. Guinness records include Kenta Adachi's 651 consecutive pull-ups in 2022 and 1,224 in 2024 [1].

According to Wikipedia, the trapezius, infraspinatus and brachialis are most active at the start of the movement, the latissimus dorsi, teres major and biceps peak in the middle, and the triceps and subscapularis peak at the top [1]. The latissimus dorsi is a large, flat muscle of the back that draws the upper arm toward the body and, with the arms fixed overhead, pulls the trunk upward. Vertical pulling exercises such as pull-downs, pull-ups and chin-ups are the standard ways of loading it [13].

In a 2017 study of 15 resistance-trained adults using three pull-up types at a fixed grip width and tempo, latissimus dorsi activity was about 80 to 85 percent of maximum voluntary contraction in all variations, with no significant difference. Only the middle trapezius differed, being lower in the towel version than the traditional one. The authors noted that all three exceeded the 40 to 60 percent range cited in earlier work as adequate for strength and hypertrophy, and said any variation could be used [3].

Because activation differences between common grips are modest, improvements are generally attributed to progressive overload, such as more repetitions, added load or slower tempo, as in other resistance training.
Many beginners cannot perform an unassisted pull-up; Wikipedia cites a 2003 study in college-age women in which one third completed a pull-up after a twelve-week full-body strength programme [1].

No trial identified examined whether a pull-up bar changes back width or visual proportions. The general claim that vertical pulling builds back muscle rests on resistance-training principles and on electromyography showing high lat activity across common variations [2][3]. Wikipedia's calisthenics article states that training volume matters for hypertrophy, that muscle groups respond differently to specific volumes, and cites a 2017 study reporting that calisthenics can improve posture, strength and body composition [11].

A 2026 analysis of the US Consumer Product Safety Commission's NEISS data from 2015 to 2024 estimated about 40,987 emergency department visits attributed to pull-up bar injuries, around 4,000 a year, with a peak of 5,421 in 2024. Patients were predominantly male (66.1 percent) with peaks among children aged 5 to 14 and adults aged 18 to 34, and head and facial injuries accounted for nearly half of presentations [4].

Wikipedia notes that overhead movements such as pull-ups narrow the subacromial space and carry a risk of shoulder impingement, and cites one study in which a pronated shoulder-width grip carried less impingement risk than other variations studied. Kipping pull-ups reduce upper-body muscle activation, raise core and lower-body work, and are described as a major cause of shoulder injury among CrossFit athletes [1]. A case report described palmar calluses, termed pull-up palms, in a man who had performed pull-ups for several years [5]. Doorway bars and wall mounts also carry installation and load-rating considerations.

No trials were found of pull-up bars for appearance outcomes. Related studies include electromyographic comparisons of pull-up and chin-up variations in trained adults [2] and of traditional, suspension-device and towel pull-ups [3]. A crossover study of whole-body vibration before a static pull-up bar hang measured forearm muscle activity in 15 men [6]. A study of assisted jumping used a resistance band attached to a pull-up bar [7]. Injury epidemiology is reported in an emergency department analysis [4] and a case report [5].

Pull-up bars are discussed as one of the cheapest ways to train the back and as a counterpart to pressing exercises for balanced upper-body development, with progress tracked by repetitions or added weight. Threads on bodyweight-fitness forums commonly ask about doorway bars that do not require screws or drilling.

On looksmax.org a user who trains at home because he cannot afford a gym posted a muscle-by-muscle plan built around an adjustable dumbbell and a pull-up bar, putting the combined cost at about $20 [8]. T Nation members describe home gyms built around a pull-up bar, rings, a squat stand and adjustable dumbbells [9][10].

Product types include tension-mounted doorway bars, doorframe-mounted bars that rest on the frame, wall and ceiling-mounted bars that require anchoring into studs or masonry, and freestanding stations. Considerations commonly discussed are the weight rating, whether installation is damaging to trim, grip positions and ceiling height.

timeline.event: Street workout videos begin spreading on YouTube, popularising bar training. [12]
Electromyographic comparison of pull-up and chin-up variations in trained adults is published. [2]
Study compares traditional, suspension-device and towel pull-ups. [3]
Kenta Adachi sets a Guinness record for consecutive pull-ups with 651, later improving to 1,224 in 2024. [1]
Case report describes 'pull-up palms', palmar calluses from pull-ups. [5]
Analysis of US emergency department data estimates about 41,000 pull-up bar injuries over 2015 to 2024. [4]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org and T Nation, pull-up bars are discussed as inexpensive home-training equipment, often alongside dumbbells [8][9][10].

claims.claim: A cheap dumbbell and pull-up bar are enough for home training when a gym is unaffordable
claims.believers: A looksmax.org user says he trains at home because he cannot afford a gym, and that an adjustable dumbbell (about $13) and a pull-up bar (about $8) cost about $20 together; he posts a muscle-by-muscle plan using them [8].
claims.experts: Electromyography studies in trained adults measured muscle activation during pull-up and chin-up variations, including a suspension device and a towel [2][3]. These studies did not assess long-term outcomes of a bar-and-dumbbell program.

claims.claim: Three sets to failure in an 8-12 rep range is the way to train each muscle with this equipment
claims.believers: The same plan prescribes pull-ups, rows and shrugs as three sets to failure in the 8-12 rep range, and says a bench would make it '1000% better' [8].
claims.experts: No published studies test this specific home program. The article's cited electromyography research compares exercise variations rather than set and rep schemes [2][3].

claims.claim: Pull-ups build a wider back and V-taper
claims.believers: Proponents describe vertical pulling as the main bodyweight way to widen the lats and make the waist look narrower in proportion [1].
claims.experts: The lats are loaded strongly in pull-up variations according to electromyography, and Wikipedia lists vertical pulls among standard lat exercises, but no trial has measured back width after a pull-up program [3][13].

claims.claim: Any pull-up variation works equally well
claims.believers: Calisthenics practitioners use pronated, neutral, towel and ring variations interchangeably [11][12].
claims.experts: A 2017 study reported similar lat and biceps activation across three variations, with only the middle trapezius differing [3].

claims.claim: A pull-up bar can be part of a low-cost improvised gym
claims.believers: T Nation users describe home gyms built around a pull-up bar, rings, a squat stand, an adjustable bench and budget adjustable dumbbells [9][10].
claims.experts: A 2026 analysis of U.S. emergency department data reviewed injuries related to pull-up and chin-up bars, including doorway bars, by body region and mechanism [4]. A case report describes palmar callosities associated with pull-ups [5].
